title: Real-world attack-vector regression corpus (must-refuse / must-render) wired into CI with path-succeeds assertions
threat: The defences exist but their evidence is host transcripts and locally-run Kani (nightly broken since 2026-09-06); a future refactor can silently reopen a Bybit-, LSB-024-, LSB-025- or 0x00-calldata-class hole and CI would stay green.
proposal: Add a fixture crate (host-runnable, in the default `cargo test` CI lane, not fuzz/ or nightly) with byte-exact vectors and expected verdicts: Bybit SafeTx (operation=1 to 0x9622…7242 with transfer-shaped data → REFUSE); operation=0 CALL to a MultiSend address → loud blind, never per-record; LSB-024 shape: 257-element array descriptor → REFUSE (MAX_ARRAY_RENDER); LSB-025: approve vs transfer with identical args → distinct intents, trailing byte → REFUSE; Ledger 1.22.0 single-byte 0x00 calldata → NOT a value transfer; LSB-020 odd-length-hex uint → companion-side canonicalisation test; Radiant transferOwnership/swapOwner → Danger class; Permit2 domain submitted as kind 2 without descriptor → REFUSE; same inputs under `ui-px` (make e2e-px) and legacy. Each test asserts the SUCCESS/REFUSAL path was actually taken (status code + page banner), per the repo's 'green can mean never ran' lesson.
rationale: Ledger's LSB-024 timeline (fix merged 2026-05-05, tagged release shipped without it) and Trezor's admission that signature-only fixtures cannot distinguish clear from blind paths are both process failures a named corpus catches. pq1 has no Bybit vector and its fuzz/Kani evidence is not CI-enforced.
repo_evidence: grep -rli bybit secure/src tx/src fsbl-tests dbgen/tests → empty
fuzz/ workspace outside CI (#451); nightly Kani not completing (#776); CI enforcement found advisory (#456)

vendor_precedent: Ledger app-ethereum release notes 1.22.0/1.22.3 enumerate regression classes; Trezor tests/device_tests/ethereum/test_definitions.py:576-609 asserts the mismatch path.
risks: Fixture bytes must be real calldata (pull Bybit tx 0x46deef0f52e3a983b67abf4714448a41dd7ffd6d32d32da69d62081c68ad7882 from chain data) and checked in with provenance; stale fixtures (#532 class) need a freshness gate.
